text:
Alex: Heads-up — found a few ambiguities in the embeddings API contract while reviewing the new batching PR. TL;DR: need a quick decision on coercion, truncation behavior, and the batch "fencepost" rule so the SDKs/docs can ship.

Alex: Example payload we saw in prod tests:```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "input": ["hello", null, 123, "a very long string ... (>> token limit)"]
}
```

Alex: Questions: 1) How do we treat non-string items (null, numbers, objects)? 2) If an item exceeds per-item token limit, do we return embedding for truncated content or return an error for that item? 3) If a batch hits the max_items_per_request (fencepost), do we accept exactly N or reject N+1? 4) Output vector shape: is it always fixed-length (e.g., 1536) and must we pad/zero for empty inputs?

Maria: Great catch. Short answers from my POV: coerced -> string; truncation -> embed truncated content (current runtime does this); fencepost -> accept up to max (reject > max); shape -> fixed-length always. But we should make these explicit in the contract.

Julian: I agree with Maria but want to call out edgecases: what about empty-string and null? Historically some clients assume empty => zeros which masks OOD detection.

Cheng: Implementation notes: runtime currently does these: - non-strings are coerced via JSON.stringify for objects, toString() for numbers/null -> yields "null" for null. - per-item token truncation is done by byte/utf8-aware tokenizer trunc to max_tokens_per_item (configured). We return embedding for truncated text, and set response field `truncated: true` in our internal logs but not surfaced in API today. - batch limit is enforced server-side: max_items_per_request = 512, requests with >512 fail 400.

Alex: OK helpful. Two followups: A) should API explicitly surface per-item `truncated` flag in the response array (per-item metadata)? B) For null/empty -> do we return zero-vector or embedding-of-"null"/""?

Sam: From product/use-cases: prefer deterministic behavior with minimal surprises for embeddings pipelines. My vote: coerce null->empty-string, empty-string -> return zero-vector of correct dim and set `is_empty: true` in per-item metadata. That helps downstream filter. For numbers/objects, coerce to string.

Julian: I like Sam's idea of returning zero-vector for empty after coercion, but important to keep vector dim same. Also good to surface `is_truncated` and `was_coerced` booleans per item for debuggability.

Maria: Concern: adding per-item metadata is a breaking shape change unless we put it under a new optional `meta` array parallel to `data`. Proposal: response stays same by default (list of vectors) but allow `include_item_meta=true` query param/arg that returns: `{ data: [vectors], meta: [ { truncated, coerced, is_empty } ] }`. Backcompat safe.

Cheng: Implementation cost: adding optional meta is doable in ~1 week backend + SDK updates. We already serialize vectors as flat floats; meta is small. Need product sign-off.

Alex: Agree on optional meta. On zero-vector semantics: we should be explicit. If original item coerces to empty-string (null -> ""), return zero-vector and set meta.is_empty true. For numbers/objects -> coerce to string and embed normally.

Maria: We'll document: - Coercion: null -> empty-string; booleans/numbers -> toString(); objects/arrays -> JSON.stringify(). - Truncation: per-item token limit = 8192 tokens; we embed truncated content and set meta.is_truncated true when include_item_meta=true. - Batch limit: max_items_per_request = 512; requests with >512 return 400. - Output: fixed vector length = 1536 floats; empty items -> zero-vector of length 1536.

Sam: Sounds good. Can someone add a one-paragraph note in the API docs and example responses? I'll ping customers if we add meta option.

Julian: I'll file the docs PR. Drafting now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 (WIP).

Cheng: I'll implement server + SDK toggles. Assigning PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567. Estimated ETA: backend + tests 5 business days, SDKs + docs another 3.

Alex: Quick code-review/ops question: for truncated items, are we OK with returning embeddings that may mismatch evaluation prompts? We should add a warning in the SDK if include_item_meta not set and (truncated items exist) to avoid silent regressions.

Maria: Good point. Suggestion: add `X-Embedding-Warnings` response header listing counts like `truncated=2, coerced=1`. Non-breaking and easy for clients to detect without meta.

Cheng: Implementable — will add that header when any non-default behavior happens (coercion/truncation/empty). header value is short csv.

Sam: ACTIONS: - @Julian: finish docs PR (include examples and decision rationale). - @Cheng: implement runtime + header + meta flag, link PR above. - @Alex: add SDK warning and unit tests for empty/null/number/object cases.

Alex: I'll open the SDK PR today and tag Cheng/Julian for review. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: build/runtime #4567 started by Cheng — status: queued

Cheng: Noting one more detail — we should add an integration test in embeddings e2e that sends a mixed-type batch and asserts: 1) 400 when >512, 2) zero-vector length 1536 for empty items, 3) header present when coercion/truncation occurred. I'll add that to PR.

Julian: Perfect. Once docs PR is ready I'll merge and ship in the next release notes.

Alex: Thanks team, closing this thread after PRs link back here.
